problem: The sweep resolved the skills root, category and skill directory by path construction, so a symlinked component let it unlink files outside the installed tree.
impact: An installed tree whose skills root, category or skill directory is a symlink (a shared checkout, a relocated tree) loses files in the link's target.
suggested_fix: Walk each path component with lstat, stop at a symlink or non-directory with a recorded outcome, and confirm containment with realpath.
evidence: Raised in round 1 against 50d2dd0c; round 2 reproduced all three cases in tmp trees and confirmed the fix (reviews/round-2-report.md).

class_scope.enumeration_method: keryx ctx rg for unlink/rm over src/gdskills/install.ts, export.ts and src/commands/update.ts, init.ts, skills.ts: unlink appears only in install.ts, in these two helpers. removeUnmodifiedRetiredRules was already lstat-first from flow 256 (#533); this one was not.

verification.evidence: All three reproductions executed in tmp trees (scratchpad/r2-257/repro.ts): symlinked skills root, symlinked category, symlinked skill dir. In every case the victim SKILL.zed.md survives, the sweep returns exactly one skipped-dir outcome with reason "symlink", and the warning names the blocked component. Category probed once, so one symlinked category yields one notice rather than 67.

disposition.evidence: 62cd9424 — the sweep walks each path component with lstat, refuses a symlinked parent and confirms containment with realpath; round 2 executed all three reproductions.

problem: Candidates were matched on a normalised name, so on a case-insensitive filesystem a user's differently-cased file satisfied the match and was removed.
impact: A user file named skill.zed.md is deleted on macOS while SKILL.zed.md is what the sweep meant.
suggested_fix: Take candidates from readdir and match the on-disk name exactly.
evidence: Raised in round 1; round 2 executed it on the case-insensitive tmp filesystem here — the sweep returns an empty list and the file survives.

class_scope.enumeration_method: The only name-matched deletion in the install path; removeUnmodifiedRetiredRules compares content hashes, not names.

verification.evidence: The tmp filesystem here is case-insensitive — existsSync("SKILL.zed.md") returns true for an on-disk skill.zed.md. With that file present the sweep returns an empty list and the file survives; readdir plus exact-name matching is what does the work.

disposition.evidence: 62cd9424 — candidates come from readdir and are matched by exact name; round 2 executed it on the case-insensitive filesystem here and the differently-cased user file survives.

problem: Removals were silent: nothing told the operator that a file had been deleted from their tree.
impact: Roughly 88 files disappear from an installed tree on upgrade with no record.
suggested_fix: Return an outcome per candidate and report removals.
evidence: Raised in round 1; round 2 confirmed a printed notice per removal. Round 2 then found the reporting landed under the wrong heading (NEW-2).

class_scope.enumeration_method: The one new deleting helper in this branch; the retired-rule sweep already reported its kept outcomes since flow 256.

verification.evidence: Happy path removes a genuine stale build and returns {action:"removed"}, rendered as a printed notice. SKILL.md, SKILL.detail.md and reference.md are untouched; a symlink as the candidate file gives kept-not-regular-file with the target intact.

disposition.evidence: 62cd9424 — the sweep returns an outcome per candidate and removals are reported; the heading they were reported under was corrected in a91679b9.

problem: The anatomy:length finding told the author to raise the ceiling, while skills-storage-workflow.mdc forbids raising it. The tool and the rule instructed opposite actions.
impact: An author following the message violates the rule; an author following the rule cannot clear the finding.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the message to say split the skill, state that a ceiling only moves down, and have the rule quote it.
evidence: Raised in round 1; round 2 read both files and confirmed the message and the rule's blockquote now agree.

class_scope.enumeration_method: The ceiling rule is stated in exactly two places — the finding message and the storage rule, plus its byte-identical install mirror; all were read.

verification.evidence: The message at src/gdskills/bundled-eval.ts:1986 now says "Split the skill... A ceiling only ever moves DOWN"; the Length Ceilings blockquote in skills-storage-workflow.mdc matches it word for word, compared by hand. bundled-eval.test.ts:1704-1718 reads both files. The .metaproject mirror is byte-identical to the bundled copy.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 and 580dc5c2 — the message says to split the skill and that a ceiling only moves down; the rule quotes it, and a91679b9 made the test compare the quote verbatim.

problem: The routing record was a single ratio asserted as greater than 0.5, so a large regression still passed and an improvement was never recorded.
impact: The corpus could not detect the regressions it exists to detect.
suggested_fix: Record rank-1 first-place and total as integers and compare them for equality against a live recount.
evidence: Raised in round 1; round 2 confirmed toBe on both integers and that the denominator is the corpus's own counted positives.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Both routing baselines in the branch were read: ROUTING_BASELINE pins exact scores per entry and was already exact; the corpus ratio was the loose one.

verification.evidence: RANK1_FIRST=285 and RANK1_TOTAL=287 are both re-measured live and compared with toBe, not a bound; the denominator is the corpus's own counted positives. Lowering silently is impossible — the only escape is KNOWN_ROUTING_GAPS[].excluded, a visible registry rather than a number. bun test src/commands/routing-corpus.test.ts: 181 pass, 0 fail.

disposition.evidence: 437a6f3e — RANK1_FIRST and RANK1_TOTAL are integers compared with toBe against a live recount, so a regression and an unrecorded improvement both fail.

problem: AC11's ledger had no test, and the citation of it in skills-storage-workflow.mdc was not covered by the xref sweep, so either could rot unnoticed.
impact: The criterion could be satisfied by a file that is later deleted or renamed with nothing failing.
suggested_fix: Add a contract test pinning the ledger's existence, header and append-only statement, and the rule's citation of it.
evidence: Raised in round 1; round 2 confirmed three tests at bundled-eval.test.ts:2035-2077 and judged them sufficient for AC11.

class_scope.enumeration_method: The ledger is referenced from exactly one rule and checked by one sweep; all three sites were read.

verification.evidence: Three tests at bundled-eval.test.ts:2035-2077 pin the ledger's existence, header, separator row, the append-only statement and the rule's citation; bun test src/gdskills/bundled-eval.test.ts gives 60 pass, 0 fail. The instructed CHECKED_PATH_ROOTS change was independently re-measured: package.json files does not publish docs/skills/, so the refusal holds; the replacement is sufficient for AC11.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 — three contract tests pin the ledger and the rule's citation of it. The instructed CHECKED_PATH_ROOTS change was refused with measurement and the refusal upheld in round 2; its overstated evidence was corrected in a91679b9.

problem: The NOT-for clause was matched without a word boundary, so 'not formatted', 'not forced' and 'not fortunate' satisfied it.
impact: A skill with no NOT-for clause passes anatomy:sections.
suggested_fix: Require a word boundary after 'not for'.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed all three strings are now rejected by fixture.

verification.evidence: Fixtures reject "not formatted", "not forced" and "not fortunate"; the control with a real NOT-for clause passes. skills verify --bundled passes every check across all 67 shipped skills, so the boundary introduces no false positive.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 — a word boundary after 'not for'; fixtures reject not formatted, not forced, not fortunate.

problem: The bare-imperative list flagged nouns used as nouns — 'review', 'check' — producing false description findings.
impact: A correct description is reported as a bare imperative.
suggested_fix: Gate the noun-ambiguous verbs behind a determiner test.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed the gate and found no false positives across the 67 shipped skills.

verification.evidence: The determiner gate has its own unit test, and the sweep over the 67 shipped skills reports no description finding — the nouns that previously tripped it now pass.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 — noun-ambiguous verbs are gated behind a determiner test; no false positive across the 67 shipped skills.

problem: An anatomy finding was reported once per runtime build rather than once per skill.
impact: A skill with a Codex build reports the same missing section twice.
suggested_fix: Attribute anatomy findings to the skill.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed with a fixture carrying a Codex build: one finding, not two.

verification.evidence: A fixture skill carrying a Codex build produces exactly one anatomy:sections finding, not one per build.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 — anatomy findings are attributed to the skill; a fixture with a Codex build reports one finding.

problem: An empty Verification body satisfied anatomy:sections.
impact: A heading with nothing under it counts as an exit criterion.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed the fixture is rejected.

verification.evidence: A fixture with an empty Verification body is rejected; the control with a body passes.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 — a Verification section must have a non-empty body.

problem: A Red Flags table of placeholder rows satisfied anatomy:sections.
impact: A table copied without content counts as a Red Flags table.
suggested_fix: Add a substance floor for rows.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed placeholder rows are rejected.

verification.evidence: A fixture whose Red Flags rows are placeholders is rejected; the shipped tree passes, so the floor does not fire on real tables.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 — Red Flags rows carry a substance floor; placeholder rows are rejected.

problem: Two skills could ship the same Red Flags table with nothing noticing.
impact: A backfill that copies one skill's table into another passes every check.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed the check exists, is attributed to the later key, and the shipped tree is clean.

verification.evidence: anatomy:red-flags-collision exists, fires on a fixture pair sharing a table, is attributed to the later key only, and reports nothing on the shipped tree.

disposition.evidence: ce8e43c9 — new anatomy:red-flags-collision check, attributed to the later key; the shipped tree is clean.

problem: The NOT-for clause named a skill that does not exist in the catalog.
impact: The clause routes a reader to nothing.
suggested_fix: Name the skill that owns the excluded case.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed interview and interviewer both exist, so the clause resolves.

verification.evidence: Both interview and interviewer are present in the catalog, so the rewritten NOT-for clause resolves to a skill that exists.

disposition.evidence: 580dc5c2 — the NOT-for clause names interview, which exists in the catalog.

problem: The skill quoted output that keryx review reviewers does not produce.
impact: An agent following the skill compares against a format that never appears.
suggested_fix: Quote the real row, including the no-recorded-origin case.
evidence: Round 2 matched the quoted row against src/review/reviewers.ts:200-205 exactly.

verification.evidence: The quoted row in reviewer-skill-creator matches src/review/reviewers.ts:200-205 exactly, including the "no recorded origin" case for drift === "none".

disposition.evidence: 580dc5c2 — the quoted row matches src/review/reviewers.ts:200-205 exactly, including the no-recorded-origin case.

problem: The skill passed a flow id to keryx flow check, which takes none.
evidence: Round 2 ran keryx flow check and confirmed it takes no id.

verification.evidence: keryx flow check was run: it takes no flow id, so the argument the skill used to pass was wrong and its removal is correct.

disposition.evidence: 580dc5c2 — the flow id was dropped; keryx flow check takes none.

problem: The rule did not say what makes a runtime build genuinely differ, so the criterion for keeping one was unstated.
impact: A future author cannot tell whether a per-runtime copy is justified.
suggested_fix: Enumerate the two cases and name the skills that qualify.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed both cases are enumerated and the seven gproject skills named.

verification.evidence: The storage rule now enumerates both divergence cases — different instructions, different metadata.compatible_harnesses — and names the seven gproject skills that qualify; 15 runtime builds remain in the tree, consistent with that list.

disposition.evidence: 580dc5c2 — the rule enumerates the two divergence cases and names the seven gproject skills.

problem: The export manifest still carried usedFallbackBuild after T5 removed the fallback concept.
impact: A consumer reads a field that no longer means anything.
suggested_fix: Remove it and bump schemaVersion, with a test tying the two.
evidence: Round 2 confirmed schemaVersion 2 with a pinning assertion and no usedFallbackBuild in shipped code.

verification.evidence: schemaVersion is 2 with a pinning assertion, and no usedFallbackBuild reference remains in shipped code (only comments and journals). export-runtime-builds.test.ts is part of the 130 pass / 0 fail run.

disposition.evidence: 5eee9eed and 580dc5c2 — usedFallbackBuild removed and schemaVersion bumped to 2, tied together by a test.

problem: Several skills carried only one paraphrase, so a single wording change could move the record without a real routing regression.
impact: The corpus measures wording rather than routing for those skills.
suggested_fix: Require at least two paraphrases per skill.
evidence: Round 2 scored all 48 added paraphrases: 48 of 48 rank their own skill first and none quotes its own triggers.

verification.evidence: Every positive added by 437a6f3e was extracted and scored: 48 of 48 rank their own skill first and 0 quote any of their own triggers verbatim; triggers are present on the catalog entries, so the no-quoting check is non-vacuous.

disposition.evidence: 437a6f3e — every skill carries at least two paraphrases; all 48 added were scored and each ranks its own skill first.
